text:
anya: Thinking out loud — current token-bucket + global leaky window is starving small keys during microbursts. Proposal: per-key short queues + proportional fair dequeue + a very short decay (200-500ms) so we absorb microbursts without blowing steady-state quotas.

kiran: can you sketch how that interacts with per-org vs per-key quotas? i.e. if an org sends 100 keys, do we backpressure the org or the hot keys?

anya: primary idea is backpressure at key-level first. if a single key exceeds queue depth, we shed that key (503-ish) but we also surface metrics that let the org-level controller scale. only when many keys are hot do we apply org-level rate limiting to avoid noisy-neighbor collapse.

sam: sounds reasonable. how do we avoid head-of-line blocking? small keys shouldnt get stuck behind a long request.

anya: using priority FIFO with a fast-path for <128-token requests; these get expedited. also dequeue uses proportional fairness algorithm so keys with small outstanding work still get slices.

matt: config sketch i threw together:
```yaml
burst_shaper:
  per_key_queue_size: 8
  per_key_decay_ms: 300
  expedited_threshold_tokens: 128
  org_fallback_threshold: 0.7 # pct of org tokens alloc to trigger org-level flow
  shed_response: 503
```

jen: what metrics do we need to monitor during rollout? we should be able to detect unintended rejections quickly.

sam: at minimum: `quota.per_key_queue_depth`, `quota.burst_shaper.rejections`, `quota.per_org_drop_rate`, `inflight.per_key`, and `fairness.scalar` (how much we scaled per-key). also histograms for latency pre/post expedite.

kiran: do we keep token-bucket as a long-window guard? token bucket is nice for steady-state billing control.

anya: yes — token-bucket stays for steady-state. This shaper is a short-term microburst layer sitting in front of token bucket. Order: accept -> per-key queue/shaper -> token-bucket -> serve. Shaper drops fast, token-bucket enforces longer windows.

matt: any thought about client-visible errors? If we return 503 often, SDKs should surface `retry-after` with jitter. We can add `x-redwood-shard` header to help debugging.

jen: rollout plan suggestion: canary on dev-orgs (internal + 3 customers) for 48h with flags: `burst_shaper.enabled` and `burst_shaper.log_verbose=true`. If rejections spike -> auto-disable.

ops-bot: alert rule draft: `sum by(org) (quota.burst_shaper.rejections[1m]) > 5` -> pager if sustained >5m. Otherwise page to #oncall if >100 org rejections in 1m.

sam: edge case: very bursty but legitimate workloads (batch evals). need an allowlist for keys that have opt-in high-burst policy and are billed differently.

anya: agreed — include `burst_profile: "high"` tag on API keys (account req) so ops can give different queue sizes. not automatic.

kiran: one more: how do we test fairness algorithm? can we simulate 10k keys with Zipf distribution and measure tail latencies and per-key drop rates?

matt: i already have a load-gen branch that does that. results: with proposed params tail p95 latency drops but p99 for tiny keys slightly up unless expedited threshold present. i can push perf plots.

jen: ok next steps: matt push config PR behind feature flag, sam add dashboards & SLOs, eng-oncall add alert rules, kiran + anya validate canary list, then 48h canary.

anya: thanks — i'll open the PR and add the design note. tagging @kiran for architecture review. :thumbsup:

kiran: lgtm, would like to review the fairness math (PF slice) before merge.

matt: will add comments and test artifacts in PR.

anya: cool. if we see regressions we fallback by toggling `burst_shaper.enabled=false` (no deploy needed).

jen: also add a console toggle so sales/support can disable for a customer during incident.

ops-bot: noted: runbook entry created: `docs/runbooks/burst_shaper_fallback.md`

sam: leaving a reminder to correlate cost impact: `tokens_saved_by_caching` vs `tokens_dropped_by_shaper` so finance can see the tradeoff.

anya: great call. i'll add that metric to the dashboard.

matt: pushing a short perf snapshot to the PR in ~30m.

kiran: thanks all. moving to close the thread unless more feedback in the PR.
